name: Washington
permitAge: 15 if enrolled in an approved driver training course; 15 and a half otherwise (Driver Guide §1.8, RCW 46.20.055)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours: 40 daytime and 10 at night, supervised by a licensed driver with 3 or more years of experience (Driver Guide §1.8; RCW 46.20.075 adds: supervisor at least 21)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months (Driver Guide §1.8); permit valid 1 year, renewable (§1.8)
teen.nightLimit: Intermediate license: no driving 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. unless with a parent, guardian or licensed driver 25 or older (§1.8); RCW 46.20.075 also allows school, religious or employment activities; agricultural driving exempt; ends after 1 year of safe driving
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate license: first 6 months no passengers under 20 except immediate family; after that no more than 3 non-family passengers under 20 (Driver Guide §1.8, RCW 46.20.075)
teen.phone: Permit and intermediate holders: no phone or wireless device at all, hands-free included, except to report an emergency (§1.8, §3.0). All drivers: may not hold any electronic device while driving (§3.4), including when stopped in traffic or at a light (RCW 46.61.672).

notes: Handbook: Washington Driver Guide, DOL form 520-400 (R/4/25), English; plain-text PDF dated 2025-06-30, read in full 2026-10-09. Spanish guide 520-401 (R/4/25). The guides have no printed page numbers; questions cite section labels (e.g. §1.8), the same in the graphic and plain-text PDFs.
Knowledge test: 40 questions, 32 correct to pass; passing score valid 2 years; offered in 12 languages (DOL test page). Test size and pass mark are not in the handbook.
Supervisor for permit holders: driving instructor or licensed driver with at least 5 years of experience, in the seat beside the driver (RCW 46.20.055; seat rule not in handbook).
License before 18 requires a driver training course; without one, a 15½-year-old can get a permit but must wait until 18 for the license (§1.8). Intermediate license from 16.
Under 21: 0.02 BAC and any active THC are offenses (§1.15, RCW 46.61.503).
Move Over / emergency zone: move over or slow to at least 10 mph below the limit, never over 50 mph (§4.17); zone is 200 feet before and after (RCW 46.61.212).
Left turn on red onto a one-way street after stopping, unless a sign prohibits (§4.11); RCW 46.61.055 adds: from a one-way or two-way street.
From November 1, 2026, first-time license applicants under 25 must pass a free online work zone and first responder safety course (DOL test page; RCW 46.20.075(1)(d)). Not in the R/4/25 handbook.
